PAPERS.title: Post-operative exposure to air pollution and colorectal cancer survival: A multi-center cohort study in southwestern China.
PAPERS.short: Chongqing 7068 post-resection CRC patients: PM2.5 HR 1.079 per 5 ug/m3 for all-cause death; organic matter the consistent constituent
PAPERS.pm: CHAP residential PM2.5, PM10 and gases; TAP PM2.5 constituents (SO4, NO3, NH4, OM, BC); 1-year lagged moving averages, time-varying
PAPERS.endpoint: All-cause mortality after radical colorectal cancer resection
PAPERS.affil: First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, China; First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: 7,068 patients after radical colorectal cancer resection at four Chongqing hospitals, median follow-up 56 months, 1,540 deaths; residential CHAP PM2.5, PM10 and gases and TAP PM2.5 constituents; time-varying Cox models on 1-year lagged moving averages. Per 5 ug/m3, HR 1.079 (95% CI 1.045-1.115) for PM2.5 and 1.050 (1.027-1.074) for PM10, stable in two-pollutant and sensitivity models. Organic matter was the most consistent constituent (HR per IQR 1.088, 1.028-1.152), robust in residual and remaining-mass models; O3 was inversely associated. Weakness: all-cause rather than CRC-specific death, residence at diagnosis only, and stage and treatment can be confounded by hospital catchment; constituent surfaces are model products with correlated errors. Relevance: the OM signal argues for organic-aerosol-sensitive monitoring, which optical mass sensors do not resolve.

PAPERS.title: Blood pressure and arterial stiffness in the pathway between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular risk: exploratory mediation analysis in middle-aged and older adult men.
PAPERS.short: Varese RoCAV men: +151 MACE per 100,000 p-y per 1 ug/m3 PM2.5, 32% mediated by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity
PAPERS.pm: 12-month mean residential PM2.5 before baseline from EXPANSE models; per 1 ug/m3
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident major acute CHD or stroke (MACE); mediation by blood pressure and cfPWV
PAPERS.affil: University of Insubria, Italy; University of Insubria, Italy
PAPERS.n: 2,119 men aged 50-75 free of CHD and stroke in the Varese RoCAV cohort, cfPWV measured in 1,015; 12-month pre-baseline PM2.5 from EXPANSE models; median follow-up 7.6 years, 178 MACE; marginal structural and Aalen models. Each 1 ug/m3 PM2.5 was associated with 151 (95% CI 21-282) additional MACE per 100,000 person-years, 48 (17-79) of them mediated by cfPWV (32%); systolic BP and pulse pressure each mediated about 16%. The cfPWV-mediated excess was larger with impaired glucose (96, 38-155) and raised LDL (88, 28-147). Weakness: men only, one year of exposure, mediators measured at baseline alongside exposure so temporal ordering is assumed, and wide CIs from 178 events. Relevance: arterial stiffness as a measurable intermediate makes smaller sensor-based exposure cohorts feasible.

PAPERS.title: Harmonizing measurements of oxidative potential of PM: an interlaboratory comparison of the ascorbic acid assay
PAPERS.short: 26-laboratory comparison of ascorbic-acid oxidative potential: repeatable within labs, significant between-lab discrepancies, just over half satisfactory
PAPERS.pm: Four PM filter samples and one chemical standard; simplified OP-AA protocol covering extraction to calculation
PAPERS.endpoint: Inter-laboratory agreement of OP-AA measurements
PAPERS.affil: Universite Grenoble Alpes, CNRS, IGE, France; Universite Grenoble Alpes, CNRS, IGE, France
PAPERS.n: Second international oxidative-potential inter-laboratory comparison, after the 2023 DTT exercise: 26 laboratories measured ascorbic-acid OP (OP-AA) on four PM filter samples and one chemical compound with a simplified protocol covering the whole chain including extraction. Most laboratories were internally repeatable, but between-laboratory discrepancies were significant; just over half achieved satisfactory results, which the authors take as evidence the protocol is fit for large-scale use. Technical, analytical and calculation refinements are also tested. Weakness: the abstract gives no z-scores, between-laboratory CVs or magnitude of the discrepancies, and four samples span a limited OP range. Relevance: OP is now a recommended monitoring metric in the revised EU Air Quality Directive; harmonised AA and DTT protocols are the precondition for validating any sensor-based or proxy OP estimate.

PAPERS.title: Smoke, Not Smoking, as a Possible Risk Factor Triggering Conversion in Leber's Hereditary Optic Neuropathy: A Retrospective Case Series.
PAPERS.short: LHON carriers in Northern California wildfire smoke: 7/9 converted vs 8/31 elsewhere (OR 10.1, p=0.02); four cases 4-8 weeks post-fire
PAPERS.pm: Wildfire smoke assigned by region of residence and multi-day AQI >150 (2017 Wine Country, 2018 Camp Fire); no individual PM2.5
PAPERS.endpoint: Conversion of LHON mutation carriers to symptomatic bilateral vision loss
PAPERS.affil: Doheny Eye Institute, USA; David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA, USA
PAPERS.n: Retrospective case series plus exploratory registry analysis. Four genetically confirmed LHON carriers developed bilateral vision loss 4-8 weeks after the 2017 Wine Country and 2018 Camp Fire smoke episodes, all living where AQI exceeded 150 for consecutive days; two had been asymptomatic for over four decades. In the 40-carrier registry, conversion in 2017-2018 was 7/9 (78%) in the wildfire-affected region vs 8/31 (26%) elsewhere (OR 10.1, Fisher p=0.02, no CI); within 8 weeks of the Camp Fire, 3/5 vs 0/23. Weakness: tiny numbers, region of residence as the only exposure, and a 26% background conversion in two years far above usual LHON penetrance suggests registry selection. Relevance: a mitochondrial-susceptibility signal that would need individual smoke PM2.5 to test - the use case for dense sensor networks during fires.

PAPERS.title: Association of early-life particulate matter exposure with childhood carotid intima-media thickness: identification of sensitive windows and exploratory analysis of vitamin D status.
PAPERS.short: Wuhan 990 children: early-life PM2.5/PM10 with thicker carotid IMT (ICA 8.49%); sensitive windows in the first postnatal year
PAPERS.pm: Pregnancy and first-postnatal-year PM2.5 and PM10 at weekly resolution (estimation method and increment not in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Childhood carotid intima-media thickness (common and internal carotid)
PAPERS.affil: Hubei Key Laboratory of Occupational Hazard Identification and Control, Wuhan, China; Wuhan Asia General Hospital, China
PAPERS.n: 990 children aged 2-14 enrolled in Wuhan, December 2023-July 2024; pregnancy and first-postnatal-year PM2.5 and PM10; generalized linear models and weekly distributed-lag non-linear models. Early-life PM was associated with thicker cIMT, percent changes from 2.67% (95% CI 0.35-5.04) to 9.98% (4.37-15.89); internal carotid exceeded common carotid (PM2.5 8.49%, 3.09-14.17 vs 2.87%, 0.71-5.09). Sensitive windows were postnatal weeks 11-17 and 48-52 for CCA and 6-22 for ICA. No PM x vitamin D interaction was significant. Weakness: one cIMT measurement years after exposure, wide age range, residential history reconstructed retrospectively, and exposure model and increment not stated in the abstract. Relevance: week-resolved infant windows are where home-level sensing would outperform annual surfaces.

PAPERS.title: Long-term exposure to particulate matter and the risk of stroke in Chinese adults: findings from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS).
PAPERS.short: CHARLS 7203 adults 45+: PM10 HR 1.144 per 10 ug/m3 for stroke; ammonium, BC and sulfate drive the PM2.5 component mixture
PAPERS.pm: Annual PM10, PM2.5 and PM2.5 components from satellite-based machine-learning estimates
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident stroke
PAPERS.affil: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University, China; First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University, China
PAPERS.n: 7,203 CHARLS participants aged 45+, 2011-2018, mean follow-up 7.88 years (56,734 person-years), 5.1% incident stroke; annual PM10, PM2.5 and PM2.5 components from satellite-based machine-learning estimates; Cox models, restricted cubic splines and quantile g-computation. PM10 was linearly associated with stroke (HR 1.144 per 10 ug/m3, 95% CI 1.101-1.188); PM2.5 and its components were non-linear. A simultaneous one-quantile increase in all components gave a 1.439-fold risk, with ammonium, black carbon and sulfate the main contributors. Weakness: stroke is self-reported physician diagnosis, the spatial resolution of exposure assignment is not stated, the PM10 HR is large relative to the literature, and the joint-effect CI is not in the abstract. Relevance: BC and sulfate as drivers again point to component-resolving measurement beyond optical mass.

PAPERS.title: Population-weighted and area-weighted ambient PM(2.5) and O(3) concentrations in China from 2015 to 2024.
PAPERS.short: China 2015-2024: population-weighted PM2.5 53.1 to 31.3 ug/m3 (-2.51/yr), 6-10 ug/m3 above area-weighted; O3 rising
PAPERS.pm: CHAP v4 annual PM2.5 and v3 MDA8 O3 rasters linked to WorldPop population counts
PAPERS.endpoint: Population- vs area-weighted annual PM2.5 and O3, national and 0.2-degree trends
PAPERS.affil: Affiliated Panyu Central Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University, China; Second People's Hospital of Panyu District, China
PAPERS.n: Annual ChinaHighAirPollutants PM2.5 (v4) and MDA8 O3 (v3) rasters linked to WorldPop population counts, 2015-2024. Population-weighted PM2.5 fell from 53.06 to 31.25 ug/m3 (slope -2.51 ug/m3 per year, 95% CI -3.16 to -1.87) and area-weighted from 42.69 to 24.83; population-weighted O3 rose from 77.06 to 96.75 ug/m3 (+1.99 per year, 1.19-2.79). Population weighting added about 6-10 ug/m3 to national PM2.5; spatial slopes were stable at 0.1-0.25 degree aggregation. Weakness: descriptive only, and the CHAP product's own error, larger where monitors are sparse, is not propagated into the trends. Relevance: the persistent population-versus-area gap is the argument for siting networks by population rather than by area.

PAPERS.title: Long-term PM(2.5) trends and spatial heterogeneity over Delhi-NCR: insights from detrending and meteorological normalization.
PAPERS.short: Delhi-NCR 38 sites 2017-2024: deweathered PM2.5 down 18.75% since 2018; secondary 46.6%; short-term variance 68-70%
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 and PM10 at 38 regulatory sites; ERA5 ventilation-coefficient normalisation, KZ decomposition, primary/secondary fractionation
PAPERS.endpoint: Meteorologically normalised PM trends and spatial hotspots
PAPERS.affil: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, India; Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, India
PAPERS.n: PM2.5 and PM10 at 38 Delhi-NCR monitoring sites (traffic, residential, industrial, commercial), 2017-2024, normalised with an ERA5 ventilation coefficient and decomposed with Kolmogorov-Zurbenko filtering, with primary/secondary fractionation and geospatial analysis. Winter and post-monsoon PM2.5 averaged 168 and 161 ug/m3 vs 43 in the monsoon. The annual ventilation coefficient rose 35%; deweathered PM2.5 fell 18.75% from 2018 to 2024, with both primary and secondary fractions declining; secondary PM2.5 was 46.6% overall. Short-term variability carried 68-70% of variance; post-COVID reductions of 10-30% were widespread but hotspots persisted. Weakness: no uncertainty on the trend, fractionation method not described in the abstract, uneven site completeness. Relevance: with short-term variance dominant, network density and temporal resolution set exposure accuracy in Delhi.

PAPERS.title: Assessment of Particulate Matter Emissions from Corn-Milling Sites in Cape Coast Metropolitan, Southern Ghana
PAPERS.short: Cape Coast milling markets, 10 months of IQAir optical PM: PM2.5 27-29 ug/m3, WHO 24-h exceeded on 61-92% of days (preprint)
PAPERS.pm: IQAir AirVisual Outdoor optical monitors at 1.5 m, 5-minute PM1, PM2.5, PM10, March-December 2024
PAPERS.endpoint: Concentrations, guideline exceedance and EPA-method hazard quotients at grain and spice milling markets
PAPERS.affil: University of Cape Coast, Ghana; University of Cape Coast, Ghana
PAPERS.n: Research Square preprint, not peer reviewed. Ten-month deployment (March-December 2024) of IQAir AirVisual Outdoor optical monitors at breathing height at two informal milling markets in Cape Coast, 5-minute PM1, PM2.5 and PM10. Mean PM2.5 was 27.0 and 28.9 ug/m3, above the WHO 24-h guideline on 61% and 92% of days; mean PM10 53.5 and 57.5 ug/m3. Peaks tracked grain milling (June-August) and spice milling (December); hazard quotients were 1.80 and 1.93 for PM2.5. Weakness: uncorrected optical sensors in coarse organic dust with no gravimetric or reference co-location reported and humidity not addressed; HQs against ambient guidelines are not occupational limits. Relevance: direct - a long low-cost deployment in an unmonitored African setting that shows the calibration gap for non-urban aerosol types.

PAPERS.title: Assessment of Particulate Matter Pollution in Mining Communities in Southwestern Ghana
PAPERS.short: Southwestern Ghana mining community vs background, 6-9 months of IQAir PM: Akoon highest (PM10 to 121 ug/m3); humidity episodes (preprint)
PAPERS.pm: IQAir monitor PM1, PM2.5, PM10 at three sites for 6-9 months
PAPERS.endpoint: Spatial and temporal PM variation and meteorological drivers
PAPERS.affil: University of Cape Coast, Ghana; University of Cape Coast, Ghana
PAPERS.n: Research Square preprint, not peer reviewed, from the same Cape Coast group. IQAir monitors recorded PM10, PM2.5 and PM1 for 6-9 months at three southwestern Ghana sites: an artisanal gold-mining community (Akoon), Mile 7 and a background site (Agric Hill). Akoon was highest (PM10 up to 121 ug/m3); humidity above 87% and stable high pressure coincided with episodes, and a November peak occurred despite favourable dispersion. Temperature, humidity and pressure explained 51-62% of variance; high PM1/PM2.5 ratios were read as a fine-particle contribution. Weakness: optical monitors without reported correction, so part of the humidity association is likely hygroscopic-growth artefact; one monitor per site, unequal record lengths. Relevance: above 85% RH uncorrected consumer optical readings inflate, so the meteorological result is confounded by the instrument.

PAPERS.title: Impact of improved biomass stove intervention on PM-bound PAHs: concentration, size distribution, and health risk
PAPERS.short: Xuanwei improved-stove intervention: indoor PM2.5-bound PAHs 31.5 to 21.2 ng/m3 with gasifier stoves; BaP-eq and ILCR down ~32.5%
PAPERS.pm: Size-resolved indoor PM-bound PAHs before and after replacing traditional stoves with three improved types
PAPERS.endpoint: Indoor PM2.5-bound PAHs, PAH size distribution, BaP-equivalent concentration and incremental lifetime cancer risk
PAPERS.affil: Kunming University of Science and Technology, China; Peking University, China
PAPERS.n: Rural Xuanwei, Yunnan: traditional biomass stoves replaced with three improved types, indoor PM-bound PAHs measured by particle size before and after. PM2.5-bound PAHs fell most with gasifier stoves (31.52 +/- 15.44 to 21.19 +/- 1.91 ng/m3), with stove-fuel-specific shifts in size distribution; BaP-equivalent concentrations and estimated incremental lifetime cancer risk fell 32.5% with gasifiers. Weakness: before-after design without concurrent controls, so season and fuel are confounded; household numbers and sampling durations are not in the abstract; ILCR rests on default exposure factors. Relevance: PAH reductions are invisible to mass sensors; stove trials should pair optical PM with a composition or black-carbon proxy.

PAPERS.title: Organic molecular markers for offline atmospheric particulate matter source apportionment: A comprehensive review
PAPERS.short: Review of 142 studies: organic molecular markers sharpen offline PM source apportionment; diagnostic ratios undermined by inconsistent reference ranges
PAPERS.pm: Organic molecular markers and diagnostic ratios in filter-based PM; PMF and other receptor models
PAPERS.endpoint: Performance and gaps of organic-marker source apportionment
PAPERS.affil: Universite du Littoral Cote d'Opale, France; Universite du Littoral Cote d'Opale, France
PAPERS.n: Review of 142 studies on organic molecular markers (OMM) in offline PM source apportionment, covering diagnostic markers and ratios and receptor models that include organic compounds. Adding OMM improves source resolution and separation of overlapping sources relative to inorganic-only inputs; PMF is the dominant model. Diagnostic ratios remain useful for quick combustion attribution but suffer from inconsistent reference ranges and neglect of atmospheric transformation of the marker compounds. Gaps: incomplete OM characterisation and limited, non-harmonised marker sets. Weakness: no stated search protocol and no quantitative comparison of apportionment performance in the abstract. Relevance: sensor networks infer sources only through covariance with gases; OMM-resolved filter campaigns are the ground truth against which those sensor-based source signatures should be tested.

PAPERS.title: Molecular composition of wintertime haze over the northern Indian Ocean suggests extensive atmospheric processing during transport
PAPERS.short: Maldives Climate Observatory winter haze by AMS + FIGAERO-CIMS: uniform, sulfate ~48% of NR-PM1, highly oxygenated OA, 18 S-organics
PAPERS.pm: Aerosol mass spectrometer non-refractory PM1 and FIGAERO-CIMS molecular composition at a receptor site
PAPERS.endpoint: Molecular composition and atmospheric processing of submicron outflow aerosol
PAPERS.affil: not stated; Stockholm University, Sweden
PAPERS.n: Winter high-time-resolution measurements at the Maldives Climate Observatory, Hanimaadhoo, with an aerosol mass spectrometer and FIGAERO-CIMS, characterising the South Asian outflow haze at molecular level. Composition was remarkably uniform despite varying source regions and loading, indicating strong regional mixing; sulfate was about 48% of non-refractory submicron mass; 18 sulfur-containing organics were identified, some for the first time at this site; organic aerosol was highly oxygenated with prominent dicarboxylic acids. Weakness: one receptor site and season, no quantitative source apportionment in the abstract, and FIGAERO-CIMS sensitivities for many species are uncertain. Relevance: indirect - aged, sulfate-dominated, highly hygroscopic outflow is the aerosol for which humidity corrections derived over land will bias optical sensors.

PAPERS.title: Measurement report: Tethered balloon observations of vertically resolved aerosol size distributions during the U.S. DOE ARM CoURAGE and BNF campaigns
PAPERS.short: ARM tethered balloon with miniature SEMS: 63 vertical size-distribution profiles (10-300 nm); NPF particles stored in residual layer overnight
PAPERS.pm: Miniature scanning electrical mobility spectrometer on the DOE ARM tethered balloon, 10-300 nm number size distributions to ~1200 m
PAPERS.endpoint: Vertical structure of aerosol number size distribution in and above the boundary layer
PAPERS.affil: not stated; University at Albany, State University of New York, USA
PAPERS.n: A miniature scanning electrical mobility spectrometer flew on the DOE ARM tethered balloon during the 2025 CoURAGE and Bankhead National Forest campaigns, yielding 63 particle number size-distribution profiles (10-300 nm) from the surface to about 1,200 m. Profiles were homogeneous under efficient boundary-layer mixing and layered under incomplete mixing or elevated plumes; above the boundary layer they resolved transitions into the free troposphere and nocturnal residual layer. On 27 March 2025, new-particle-formation products were preserved overnight in the residual layer and mixed down the next morning. Weakness: number not mass, a 10-300 nm window, and tethered operation limited by weather. Relevance: residual-layer mixing-down explains morning surface jumps that ground networks and their ML forecasts tend to attribute to local sources.

PAPERS.title: Physicochemical evolution of transported mineral dust over northern China: evidence from field sampling and laboratory analysis during haze episodes.
PAPERS.short: Spring 2022 Asian dust over northern China: coarse dust acquires sulfate/nitrate coatings and acts as a multiphase reactor (qualitative)
PAPERS.pm: Transported coarse mineral dust sampled during dust events; bulk composition, FE-SEM single-particle morphology, ion chromatography
PAPERS.endpoint: Physicochemical ageing of dust: secondary coatings, morphology, catalytic metal content
PAPERS.affil: Southwest University of Science and Technology, China; Southwest University of Science and Technology, China
PAPERS.n: Field sampling during spring 2022 Asian dust events over northern China with laboratory analyses: source apportionment, bulk composition, FE-SEM single-particle imaging and ion chromatography. Coarse dust carried reactive calcite and clay frameworks and Fe and Mn; individual particles acquired secondary coatings dominated by sulfate and nitrate, which the authors interpret as dust acting as a multiphase reactor for heterogeneous SO2 and NOx oxidation rather than contributing directly to fine PM. Weakness: the abstract reports no quantities (coating fractions, uptake coefficients, sample numbers), so the oxidation-capacity claim is qualitative and inferred from composition, not measured kinetics. Relevance: coated, hygroscopic coarse dust is where optical low-cost sensors err most - undercounting coarse mass while humidity growth inflates readings.

PAPERS.title: Influence of Nonpolar Amino Acids on Phase Transitions of Atmospheric Aerosol Particles.
PAPERS.short: Nonpolar amino acids lower separation RH and can crystallise into three-phase particles in ammonium sulfate/organic droplets
PAPERS.pm: Ternary droplets of ammonium sulfate, a nonpolar amino acid and 2-methylglutaric acid or 1,2,6-hexanetriol; optical and Raman microscopy
PAPERS.endpoint: Separation and efflorescence relative humidity, morphology and phase state
PAPERS.affil: Pennsylvania State University, USA; Pennsylvania State University, USA
PAPERS.n: Optical and Raman microscopy of ternary droplets of ammonium sulfate, a nonpolar amino acid and a model oxidised organic (2-methylglutaric acid or 1,2,6-hexanetriol). Raising the amino-acid fraction of the organic component lowered the separation relative humidity; in some systems the amino acid crystallised while the organic and ammonium sulfate underwent liquid-liquid phase separation, giving three phases. Efflorescence RH trends followed amino-acid solubility. Weakness: model mixtures on substrates, a narrow compound set and no numbers in the abstract; ambient organonitrogen is far more diverse. Relevance: phase state and efflorescence set the hysteresis of hygroscopic growth, which governs humidity correction of optical PM sensors; organonitrogen-rich aerosol may shift that hysteresis.

PAPERS.title: Spatially autocorrelated and clustered associations between short-term exposure to PM(2.5) and daily reported confirmed COVID-19 cases across the contiguous United States, 2020-2022.
PAPERS.short: Contiguous US: PM2.5-COVID-19 case RR 1.034 per 10 ug/m3 pooled, four spatial clusters up to 1.177; 2.06% of cases attributed
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5 per 10 ug/m3 (data source and lag not in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Daily reported confirmed COVID-19 cases
PAPERS.affil: West China School of Public Health, Sichuan University, China; West China School of Public Health, Sichuan University, China
PAPERS.n: Three-stage analysis across the contiguous United States: location-specific GAMs for daily PM2.5 and confirmed COVID-19 cases, then an estimation-error-based scan statistic and multivariate conditional meta-autoregression for spatial autocorrelation and clustering. Associations were heterogeneous (I2 67%), strongly autocorrelated (rho 0.972) and formed four clusters. Pooled RR per 10 ug/m3 was 1.0341 (95% CI 1.0308-1.0375); cluster RRs ranged from 1.0005 (0.9984-1.0026) to 1.1770 (1.1551-1.1992). About 1.76 million cases (2.06%) to June 2022 were attributed to PM2.5 above the WHO guideline. Weakness: reported cases depend on testing intensity, which co-varies with season and urbanicity; PM2.5 source and lag are not given; attribution assumes causality. Relevance: low for sensing, though the clustering method could transfer to heterogeneous network-based estimates.

PAPERS.title: A case of the Mondays? Pollution exposure and delayed care in pediatric asthma hospitalizations.
PAPERS.short: Illinois Medicaid 4.5M ZIP-days: lag 0-1 PM2.5 linked to paediatric asthma admission only on Mondays - care-seeking timing confounds lags
PAPERS.pm: Daily ZIP-code PM2.5, lag 0-1 moving average and longer windows (source not in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Paediatric asthma hospitalisation probability (Medicaid)
PAPERS.affil: Southern Illinois University School of Medicine, USA; Southern Illinois University School of Medicine, USA
PAPERS.n: More than 4.5 million ZIP-code-day observations from Illinois Medicaid, 2012-2021, linking paediatric asthma hospitalisations to daily PM2.5 and meteorology in fixed-effects logistic models, with day of week as covariate and effect modifier. Lag 0-1 PM2.5 was associated with hospitalisation probability on Mondays only; PM2.5 was higher at weekends while admissions peaked early in the week, and longer exposure windows attenuated weekday-specific associations. The abstract gives no effect sizes or CIs. Weakness: admission date is partly an access outcome, so a Monday pattern can arise from delayed presentation of weekend exacerbations; the PM2.5 source is not stated. Relevance: lag structure in short-term studies is contaminated by care-seeking rhythm; symptom diaries with personal monitors would separate onset from presentation.

PAPERS.title: Associations of ambient temperature and PM2.5 concentration with temporal variability in emergency department visits for acute gastrointestinal illnesses in central Bangkok, Thailand: a 5-year retrospective analysis.
PAPERS.short: Bangkok single-hospital 2018-2023: GI emergency visits rise above 139.8 ug/m3 PM2.5, amplified by heat index (no estimates in abstract)
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5 with heat index (data source not in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Emergency department visits for gastritis and gastroenteritis
PAPERS.affil: NYU Grossman School of Medicine, USA; Chulalongkorn University, Thailand
PAPERS.n: Single-hospital time series of emergency visits for gastritis and gastroenteritis in Bangkok, 2018-2023, with heat index and daily PM2.5 in GAMs and distributed-lag non-linear models, plus stratified interaction analyses. Higher heat index and PM2.5 were associated with more GI visits; risk rose only above 139.8 ug/m3 relative to the mean daily level, and stratification suggested heat amplifies the PM2.5 association; heat index below 30 C was protective. The abstract gives no RRs or CIs. Weakness: one hospital catchment, a threshold in the extreme tail reached on few days, and no described control for seasonal infectious gastroenteritis; an inhaled-PM mechanism for GI illness is speculative. Relevance: low-moderate; Bangkok's episodic peaks suit network-resolved exposure for ED-level studies.

PAPERS.title: [Air pollution and cancer mortality in municipalities of the Valparaiso Region, Chile (2009-2019)].
PAPERS.short: Valparaiso Region 2009-2019 ecological: PM10 with all-cancer mortality in Quintero, PM2.5 with stomach cancer in Vina del Mar
PAPERS.pm: Annual PM2.5, PM10 and SO2 from the national air-quality monitoring system, five municipalities
PAPERS.endpoint: Age-standardised all-cancer and stomach-cancer mortality
PAPERS.affil: Universidad de Chile, Chile; Universidad de Chile, Chile
PAPERS.n: Ecological time series for five Valparaiso Region municipalities, 2009-2019: annual SO2, PM2.5 and PM10 from the national monitoring system against age-standardised all-cancer and stomach-cancer mortality, municipality-specific Prais-Winsten models adjusting for trend and autocorrelation. Positive coefficients were isolated: PM10 with all-cancer mortality in Quintero (beta 2.81, 95% CI 1.05-4.57), PM2.5 with stomach-cancer mortality in Vina del Mar (0.55, 0.22-0.88), SO2 with stomach cancer in Catemu (0.62, 0.28-0.96); PM10 also with both outcomes among Quintero men. Weakness: eleven annual points per municipality, many municipality x pollutant x outcome tests, no latency, ecological confounding, and beta units not given. Relevance: Quintero is an industrially impacted zone where sparse regulatory monitoring is the binding constraint on exposure-response work.

PAPERS.title: Associations between ambient air pollutants and chronic pain prevalence in US children, 2023: A cross-sectional, national study.
PAPERS.short: NSCH 2023, 54,880 US children: chronic pain associated with SO2 only (aOR 1.08); PM2.5, PM10, PM10-2.5 null at state level
PAPERS.pm: State-level EPA estimates of PM2.5, PM10, PM10-2.5 plus O3, SO2, NO2, NO
PAPERS.endpoint: Parent-reported chronic or frequent pain, past 12 months
PAPERS.affil: Stanford University, USA; Stanford University, USA
PAPERS.n: 54,880 children aged 0-17 from the 2023 National Survey of Children's Health linked to state-level EPA estimates of seven pollutants including PM2.5, PM10 and PM10-2.5; survey-weighted logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, income and asthma, with FDR correction and PCA mixture scores. Chronic pain prevalence was 5.1%. Only SO2 survived correction (aOR 1.08, 95% CI 1.02-1.13); the PM fractions were not associated and mixture scores were null. Weakness: every child in a state shares one exposure value, leaving about 51 exposure units; the SO2 increment is not given; cross-sectional with parent report. Relevance: a PM null at this spatial resolution says little - it is the scale problem neighbourhood-level sensing is meant to fix.

PAPERS.title: Association between fine particulate air pollution and the risk of death from kidney cancer in Taiwan.
PAPERS.short: Taiwan 66 municipalities 2010-2023 ecological: higher PM2.5 tertile with lower kidney-cancer mortality in men; null in women
PAPERS.pm: Municipal annual PM2.5 in tertiles
PAPERS.endpoint: Age-standardised kidney-cancer mortality
PAPERS.affil: I-Shou University, Taiwan; Kaohsiung Medical University, Taiwan
PAPERS.n: Ecological study of 66 Taiwanese municipalities, 2010-2023: annual PM2.5 tertiles against age-standardised kidney-cancer mortality, adjusted for lung-cancer mortality as a smoking proxy, urbanisation, household income and physician density. Men in higher-PM2.5 municipalities had significantly lower kidney-cancer mortality; women showed no association. The abstract gives no RRs or CIs, and the authors allow chance. Weakness: ecological, no latency, and adjusting for lung-cancer mortality - itself partly caused by PM2.5 - can over-adjust and reverse signs; diagnostic access varies with urbanisation. Relevance: low; an instructive case of proxy-adjustment bias rather than evidence on PM2.5 and renal cancer.

PAPERS.title: Development of metabolic syndrome identification model by integrating Korea national health and nutrition examination survey data with regional particulate matter, air pollutants, and green environmental factors.
PAPERS.short: KNHANES 20,035 adults: metabolic-syndrome classifiers with regional air pollution reach AUC 0.64-0.67; demographics dominate
PAPERS.pm: Regional average air pollution and green space from national statistics, assigned by residence region
PAPERS.endpoint: Metabolic syndrome classification
PAPERS.affil: aSSIST University, Republic of Korea; aSSIST University, Republic of Korea
PAPERS.n: 20,035 KNHANES adults aged 30+ (2018-2022) linked to regional average air pollution and green-space data; eight classifiers (SVM, logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and three MLPs) with class weighting for imbalance. AUCs ranged 0.644-0.666; DeepMLP was highest but not significantly better than the tree ensembles by DeLong and bootstrap tests. SHAP and permutation importance ranked sex, age and education highest; the abstract gives no PM-specific contribution. Weakness: region-level exposure assigned to individuals, cross-sectional prediction rather than inference, modest discrimination; importance scores are not effects. Relevance: low; adding coarse regional PM to a classifier adds little, as expected when exposure contrast is averaged away.

PAPERS.title: Subchronic 1-nitropyrene exposure induces meibomian gland dysfunction via lipid peroxidation-mediated ferroptosis.
PAPERS.short: Topical 1-nitropyrene in mice causes meibomian gland dysfunction via ferroptosis; ferrostatin-1 rescues, PPARalpha modulates
PAPERS.pm: Topical ocular 1-nitropyrene 10 mg/mL for 14 days in mice; human meibomian gland epithelial cells in vitro
PAPERS.endpoint: Meibomian gland dysfunction, ferroptosis and lipid peroxidation markers
PAPERS.affil: Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University, China; Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: Mice received topical ocular 1-nitropyrene, a nitro-PAH constituent of diesel-derived fine particles, at 10 mg/mL for 14 days. Exposure produced meibomian gland dysfunction - duct obstruction, acinar atrophy, reduced tear secretion, corneal epithelial defects - with loss of progenitor markers (p63, Lrig1), increased keratinisation (K10), iron overload (ferritin, NCOA4) and lipid peroxidation (GSH down, MDA up). Ferrostatin-1 abolished ferroptosis and MGD; in human meibomian gland epithelial cells PPARalpha agonism and knockdown modulated 1-NP-induced ferroptosis. Weakness: a pure compound at a concentration far above plausible ocular deposition of ambient 1-NP, delivered as drops rather than particles. Relevance: low for sensing; mechanistic plausibility for ocular-surface associations reported with traffic PM.

PAPERS.title: Chronic exposure to low-concentration urban PM2.5 promotes maladaptive kidney repair after ischemic injury via mitochondrial dysfunction and lysosomal stress.
PAPERS.short: Six months of real-world urban PM2.5 in mice impairs kidney repair after ischaemic AKI: lysosomal particle deposits, senescence, fibrosis
PAPERS.pm: Six-month exposure to real-world ambient urban PM2.5 vs filtered air (concentration not in abstract)
PAPERS.geo: Not stated in record (ambient-air exposure chamber)
PAPERS.endpoint: Maladaptive repair after ischaemia-reperfusion acute kidney injury
PAPERS.affil: Amsterdam UMC, University of Amsterdam, Netherlands; Amsterdam UMC, University of Amsterdam, Netherlands
PAPERS.n: Mice given ischaemia-reperfusion acute kidney injury or sham surgery were exposed for six months to filtered air or real-world ambient urban PM2.5. Sham kidneys changed little; after injury PM2.5 promoted inflammation, microvascular rarefaction, mitochondrial injury, metabolic reprogramming and fibrosis. PM-associated elements accumulated in proximal-tubule lysosomes with lysosomal stress, lipid remodelling and tubular senescence; transcriptomic drug repurposing nominated nicotinamide, which improved mitochondrial function in PM2.5-challenged tubular cells in vitro. Weakness: no chamber concentration, dose or group sizes in the abstract, so 'low-level' cannot be checked against ambient, and nicotinamide was tested only in vitro. Relevance: identifies a post-injury susceptibility window in which modest chronic PM2.5 matters - exactly the low-concentration range where low-cost sensors are least accurate.

PAPERS.title: Burden of Ischemic Heart Disease Attributable to Particulate Matter Pollution in China From 1990 to 2021 Based on the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
PAPERS.short: GBD 2021, China 1990-2021: PM-attributable IHD ASMR AAPC -0.38 (UI crosses 0), ASDR -0.77; male burden projected to rise (preprint)
PAPERS.pm: GBD 2021 particulate matter pollution (ambient and household) exposure estimates
PAPERS.endpoint: Age-standardised IHD mortality and DALY rates attributable to PM
PAPERS.affil: Zhejiang Taizhou Hospital, China; Zhejiang Taizhou Hospital, China
PAPERS.n: Research Square preprint, not peer reviewed. GBD 2021 secondary analysis of ischaemic heart disease attributable to particulate matter pollution in China, 1990-2021, with forecasts. The age-standardised mortality rate changed little (AAPC -0.38, 95% UI -0.89 to 0.12) while the age-standardised DALY rate declined (AAPC -0.77, -1.20 to -0.34); females declined significantly on both, and the absolute burden in males is projected to rise. Weakness: wholly downstream of GBD exposure surfaces and relative-risk functions, with no new data; the forecasting method is not described in the abstract. Relevance: low; restates GBD output that a monitoring network cannot test directly.

PAPERS.title: Projections of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease incidence and its driving factors in 195 countries and territories to 2050: a modeling study.
PAPERS.short: GBD 2021 COPD to 2050: 32.3M incident cases/yr projected; eliminating ambient PM could prevent up to 30.1% (smoking 33.0%)
PAPERS.pm: GBD 2021 ambient particulate matter as a modifiable risk factor (population impact fractions)
PAPERS.endpoint: COPD incidence projections and risk-factor impact fractions
PAPERS.affil: Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, China; Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, China
PAPERS.n: GBD 2021 secondary analysis of COPD across 204 countries (1990-2021) with Joinpoint and age-period-cohort trends and Bayesian APC projections to 2050 for 195. Annual incident cases are projected at 32.3 million (95% UI 13.6-50.9) in 2050 while the age-standardised rate falls about 3%; China, India and the USA contribute nearly half. Eliminating smoking and ambient particulate pollution could prevent up to 33.0% and 30.1% of incident cases. Weakness: projections inherit GBD exposure and relative-risk assumptions, the UI spans almost fourfold, and eliminating ambient PM is a counterfactual below any achievable level. Relevance: low; a GBD restatement, though an ambient-PM share close to smoking is a useful framing number.
